content: Have you ever seen cars zooming fast on the road? Imagine you are a little turtle trying to cross a busy highway. It sounds scary, right? How can you cross safely without getting hurt?
Why do you think we have colorful lights on the road? What would happen if there were no rules for cars? Think about this carefully before we discover the answer.

content.title: The Magic Traffic Light
content.description: Red means Stop, Yellow means Wait, and Green means Go! Cars must obey these magic colors.

content: The safest place to cross the road is the Zebra Crossing. It is a path painted with black and white stripes, just like a zebra! Cars must stop when people walk on it.

question: What should you do when the traffic light turns Red?

content: Think about the last time you crossed the road. Did you hold an adult's hand? Why is holding hands important? Reflect on how it makes you feel safe.
Traffic rules keep everyone safe. Traffic Police officers work hard every day to make sure these rules are followed, just like rules in a game keep it fair.
Next time you are in a car or walking with parents, try to spot 3 traffic lights and a zebra crossing. Point them out and become a Road Safety Master!
Now imagine you are at home playing. You see a very shiny knife on the kitchen table and a box of colorful matchsticks. They look like fun toys, but are they?
What do you think could happen if you try to play with a knife or matchsticks? Can everyday objects in our home be dangerous?

content.title: Sharp Edges and Hot Fire
content.description: Knives have sharp edges that can cut our skin. Matchsticks create fire that can burn us.

content: Things like knives, scissors, and matchsticks are tools, not toys. We must stay away from sharp objects and fire to avoid getting hurt.

question: Which of these is safe to play with at home?

content: What should you do if you or your friend gets a small cut? Should you hide it? No! Always tell a grown-up immediately so they can help.
Grown-ups use a First Aid Box to clean cuts and put on a bandage. Just like cars need a mechanic when they break down, our bodies need care when we get hurt.
Never put your fingers or metal objects inside electrical sockets! Some children think it's a game, but it can give a very dangerous and painful electric shock.
Look around your room. Point out 3 things that are safe to play with and ask your parents to show you 1 thing that is unsafe to touch.
